The AI industry is about to go through a brutal shakeout — and Gartner just put a timeline on it.

This week, Gartner's chief forecaster John Lovelock told CNBC that every AI market the firm tracks is likely to collapse into a duopoly. His reasoning: compute capacity already exceeds demand, AI companies are giving away tokens and processing power through freemium models, and the entire industry is running a last-man-standing strategy. Consolidation and takeovers among AI-focused companies are not speculative — they are expected.

The timing matters. OpenAI just revised its 2026 revenue target down by $50 billion while simultaneously raising another $30 billion at a $1.3 trillion valuation. The gap between money going in and revenue coming out is getting wider, not narrower. That is the exact condition that triggers M&A waves.

For executives and founders, this changes the calculus on every AI vendor decision. The provider you build on today may get acquired by a competitor tomorrow. Your AI architecture needs to be modular and portable — with commercial agreements that include real exit clauses.

The winners of this consolidation will set enterprise AI pricing for the next decade. The strategic question is whether your organization is positioned to survive the transition or get caught in it.
